ex_ret_instr.name: ex_ret_instr
ex_ret_instr.justification: perf list (amdzen3): Retired Instructions. The kernel maps the generic PERF_COUNT_HW_INSTRUCTIONS to 0x00c0 on family 19h (amd_zen2_perfmon_event_map, selected by amd_pmu_event_map for x86 >= 0x19, arch/x86/events/amd/core.c, Linux v7.0) and sysfs events/instructions reads event=0xc0. Every layout runs the same loop, so equal instructions per increment confirm that only addresses changed.

ls_not_halted_cyc.name: ls_not_halted_cyc
ls_not_halted_cyc.justification: perf list: Cycles not in Halt; the kernel's generic PERF_COUNT_HW_CPU_CYCLES on family 19h (0x0076; sysfs events/cpu-cycles = event=0x76). User-mode cycles of the counting thread only (exclude_kernel). Cycles divided by elapsed nanoseconds gives an effective user-cycle rate, a check for frequency differences.

ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.int_cache.name: ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.int_cache
ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.int_cache.justification: perf list: Demand Data Cache Fills by Data Source, From L3 or different L2 in same CCX. A fill of this core's L1D from another core's L2 or the shared L3 is what a line moving between private caches looks like from the requesting core.

perf_list.BriefDescription: Demand Data Cache Fills by Data Source. From L3 or different L2 in same CCX

ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.lcl_l2.name: ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.lcl_l2
ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.lcl_l2.role: control: fills from the core's own L2
ls_dmnd_fills_from_sys.lcl_l2.justification: perf list: Demand Data Cache Fills by Data Source, From Local L2 to the core. SMT siblings share the L1D, so a sibling's writes need no fill from L2; a nonzero count would indicate L1D evictions rather than inter-core transfer.

perf_list.BriefDescription: Demand Data Cache Fills by Data Source. From Local L2 to the core

ls_locks.non_spec_lock.name: ls_locks.non_spec_lock
ls_locks.non_spec_lock.justification: perf list: Retired lock instructions, Non-speculative lock succeeded. The measured loop's only memory operation is a locked add; the event distinguishes the non-speculative completion path. Its microarchitectural meaning beyond that description is not claimed (no matching PPR was obtained).

perf_list.BriefDescription: Retired lock instructions. Non-speculative lock succeeded

l2_request_g1.rd_blk_x.name: l2_request_g1.rd_blk_x
l2_request_g1.rd_blk_x.justification: perf list: All L2 Cache Requests (Breakdown 1 - Common), Data cache stores. A locked add on a line this core does not hold writable must request it from L2; counts per increment measure how often that happened.

perf_list.BriefDescription: All L2 Cache Requests (Breakdown 1 - Common). Data cache stores

l2_cache_req_stat.ls_rd_blk_c.name: l2_cache_req_stat.ls_rd_blk_c
l2_cache_req_stat.ls_rd_blk_c.role: data requests that missed this core's L2
l2_cache_req_stat.ls_rd_blk_c.justification: perf list: Core to L2 cacheable request access status, Data cache request miss in L2 (all types). The generic cache-misses event on this kernel is event=0x64,umask=0x09 (L2 misses including instruction fetch), so it is an L2 count, not a last-level-cache count; this event isolates the data side.

perf_list.BriefDescription: Core to L2 cacheable request access status (not including L2 Prefetch). Data cache request miss in L2 (all types). Use l2_cache_misses_from_dc_misses instead

ls_locks.spec_lock_hi_spec.name: ls_locks.spec_lock_hi_spec
ls_locks.spec_lock_hi_spec.justification: perf list: Retired lock instructions, High speculative cacheable lock speculation succeeded. Recorded beside the non-speculative count; together they show which documented completion paths the locked adds took.

perf_list.BriefDescription: Retired lock instructions. High speculative cacheable lock speculation succeeded
